answer: A verifier named ChipGate binds admission to a passport, reading the signed NFC chip and refusing any signature already on file, so one operator cannot hold two seats. The penalty trigger is a duplicate chip signature: a repeat seat forfeits its thirty POA bond and its issuing batch is audited. A passport costs one hundred sixty dollars, a reader forty, and enrollment twenty five minutes, so N fakes cost N times two hundred dollars plus N hours. Basalt blocks are cheap by the ton, but no onyx of forged paper survives a chip check and no zenith of cloud credit buys a second identity.
